title: Region-lock migration experiment notes and operator checklist
content:
Purpose:
Run a small, controlled experiment to simulate gradual removal of 'region-lock' legacy behavior and validate the migration path for customers with strict data-residency requirements. We want to observe operator/runtime impacts, customer-level error modes, and telemetry fidelity before any broad deprecation announcement. This doc captures the plan, telemetry design, operator checklist, and known unknowns.

Background/context:
- We currently support region pin semantics (historical name: pin) used by a subset of enterprise tenants. Some internal systems still treat that as an immutable routing contract which complicates fallback logic and cross-region failover.
- Long-term objective: converge on a simpler "region-lock" abstraction (explicit owner anchor + fallback policies) that reduces coupling between placement and control plane routing decisions.
- This experiment does NOT change customer contracts; it only simulates enforcement and migration mechanics on a testbed subset of tenants.

Goals (success criteria):
1) No unexpected data egress to non-anchored regions for >99.99% of test requests.
2) Operator-visible errors and logs map unambiguously to a single signal (region_lock_violation) so support can triage quickly.
3) Migration path is friction-limited: average time-to-fix for synthetic "migrated" tenants <= 45 minutes for operator remediation; <= 24 hours for self-serve guidance completion.
4) Latency and tail SLOs degrade by <5% under experiment load.

Scope and experiment cohorts:
- Testbed cluster: private-deploy-testbed-eu (EU primary), us-west-failover, asia-sim-zone (no production traffic).
- Cohort A (smoke): 5 synthetic tenants with simple traffic patterns (short prompts, embeddings) — immediate enforcement of region-lock with soft warnings first 2 hours.
- Cohort B (realistic): 12 internal pilot tenants (low-volume, consenting customers) — receive warning banners and a 24-hour migration window where fallback occurs to nearest anchored region with telemetry tagging.
- Cohort C (operators-only): staging tenants to exercise eviction/rollback flows and KMS/HSM key residency interactions.

Operator checklist (pre-experiment):
- Confirm testbed clusters have isolated network paths and that RBAC keys used for the experiment are restricted. (owner: Maya)
- Snapshot current route tables and region-attachment records for pilot tenants. (owner: Liam)
- Enable detailed request tracing (trace-id header propagation) and add the region_lock_violation event to the trace schema. (owner: Omar)
- Update rollback playbook in runbooks repo: add new explicit commands to revoke simulated region-lock enforcement. (owner: Aisha)

Runtime/telemetry design notes:
- New event: region_lock_violation {tenant_id, request_id, effective_anchor_region, attempted_region, fallback_region, timestamp, decision_path}. We will emit as a single-line structured log plus OTEL span attribute.
- Tag: migration_experiment_v1 on all requests in cohorts A/B/C. Use routing metadata to record which policy variant was used (legacy-pin, region-lock-soft, region-lock-hard).
- Aggregate metrics to track: violation_rate, avg_time_to_resolve, fallback_count, kms_access_block_count, tail_latency_p95/p99.
- Dashboards: temporary dashboard in Console labeled "Region-lock experiment - staging" with per-tenant heatmap and alerting thresholds for violation_rate > 0.2% over 15m window.

Customer-facing communications (pilot tenants):
- Short email template in linked doc (Confluence): "Region routing experiment: what to expect". Include a clear opt-out link and a rollback SLA.
- Banner text displayed in Console: "We're testing a routing update for data residency; you may see short-lived routing fallbacks. Contact support if you need a firm region lock."

Enforcement modes and expected operator actions:
- Soft mode (initial 2 hours for Cohort A): Log violations, attach warning header X-Region-Lock-Status: soft-warning, no strict fail. Operator action: review logs and escalate if unexpected KMS alerts occur.
- Mixed mode (24-hour for Cohort B): Allow fallback but tag request with attempted_region; set rate limit on fallbacks to avoid noisy spikes. Operator action: reach out to tenant if persistent fallbacks (>1% of requests) and provide migration guidance.
- Hard mode (operators-only Cohort C): Enforce strict rejection (403 region_lock_enforced) to validate end-to-end error handling and support experience. Operator action: follow rollback playbook to disable enforcement for a tenant and clear associated caches.

Rollback and remediation playbook (concise):
1) Identify tenant_id from region_lock_violation stream.
2) Run diagnostic script: scripts/region_lock/diagnose.sh --tenant <id> (returns route history, KMS access logs, last successful anchor check).
3) If misconfiguration: patch routing table via infra-ctl: infra-ctl routes update --tenant <id> --anchor <region> --propagate
4) If operator-triggered rollback required: infra-ctl enforcement disable --experiment region-lock-v1 --tenant <id>
5) Clear edge caches: cachectl purge --tenant <id> --scope prefix
6) Validate with trace-id replay and confirm region_lock_violation no longer emitted.

KMS and crypto considerations:
- Ensure service principal used in test can't access production keys. Use separated test HSM with same key shape to exercise auth layers.
- Telemetry must not include key material; only include success/failure codes from KMS calls.

Open questions and risks (to resolve before expanding):
- How do we signal multi-anchored tenants? (action: design fallback_priority array and add to spec)
- Edge caches may hold stale affinity mappings for up to 7 minutes; naive enforcement may spur transient violations. Consider cache TTL bumpdown for experiment.
- Legal/contract risk: ensure enterprise contracts with strict residency clauses are excluded from any test cohort. (action: cross-check Sales CRM tags)
- Self-serve UI: can Console show per-tenant expected enforcement window? Draft UI copy needed.

Metrics to collect (first-order):
- per-tenant violation_count/time_window (15m/1h/24h)
- average operator time-to-acknowledge (when pager/alert fires)
- fraction of requests that experienced fallback vs hard-reject
- KMS error rate correlation with attempted_region != anchor_region

Expected timeline (provisional):
- Week 0: infra prep + telemetry schema change + operator training (3 days)
- Week 1: Cohort A smoke run (48 hours), evaluate, adjust thresholds (2 days analysis)
- Week 2-3: Cohort B pilot (7–10 days), run migrations, build support articles
- Week 4: Cohort C hard-mode stress + final runbook updates + TL signoff

Immediate next actions (owners):
- Add region_lock_violation to OTEL schema (Omar) — due 2026-01-15
- Build temporary Console dashboard and alert (Maya) — due 2026-01-22
- Draft tenant email + support FAQ (Aisha + Customer Success) — due 2026-01-18
- Prepare rollback automation test harness (Liam) — due 2026-01-20

Notes to self / ideas for follow-up experiments:
- Test an automated self-heal step that offers tenants a one-click migration to a recommended anchor region and measures conversion rate.
- Longer-term: evaluate whether region-lock metadata can be surfaced to model-level policy that prevents KV cache replication across regions.

Unresolved TODOs (short):
- Confirm legal exclusion list for pilot tenants.
- Finalize alert thresholds for violation_rate.
- Add unit tests for header X-Region-Lock-Status variations.

If you are reviewing: ping in #eng-private-deployments with the subject line: "region-lock experiment review" and reference JIRA-RES-1127.

End of notes.
